pulls.title: 8394216: RISC-V: Elide the leading membar of an LR/SC based CAS
pulls.author: zifeihan
pulls.body_excerpt: Hi, please consider. unnecessary_release() currently reuses cas_membar_elidable() to decide whether the leading MemBarRelease of a volatile CAS idiom can be dropped. That predicate is the right condition for the trailing MemBarAcquire, but it is stronger than what the leading membar actually needs, so the leading fence rw,w is kept on the LR/SC path even though the rl annotation on the sc already covers it. This change gives the leading membar its own, weaker predicate. For a cas matched c2 code: ``` fence rw, w // MemBarRelease lr.w.aq t0, (a0) bne t0, a1, 2f sc.w.rl t0, a2, (a0) bnez t0, 1b

pulls.title: 8394082: RISC-V: Remove redundant membar from C1 compareAndSet
pulls.author: zifeihan
pulls.body_excerpt: Hi, please consider. In C1, do_CompareAndSwap and do_UnsafeGetAndSet resolve through LIRGenerator::access_atomic_cmpxchg_at / access_atomic_xchg_at, which default to the MO_SEQ_CST decorator. So casw/caswu/casl (cas_int/uint/long) and atomic_op (lir_xadd/lir_xchg) all require MO_SEQ_CST. On RISC-V, MacroAssembler::cmpxchg is already emitted with acquire (on the load) and release (on the store), and the atomic_op path uses atomic_addal/atomic_xchgal, i.e. amoadd.aqrl / amoswap.aqrl. pulls.title: 8390358: HotCodeCollector can relocate never-sampled nmethod
pulls.author: eastig
pulls.body_excerpt: HotCodeCollector stores `nmethod*` pointers during sampling. Code blobs can be freed and reused for other nmethods in between sampling and relocation. As a result we can relocate never-sampled nmethod. I managed to create a test which reproduces the issue. However the test is not reliable to be added to jtreg tests. It depends on a host and OS is being run on. To avoid the issue, I use compile ids to distinguish nmethods. We need to dereference nmethod pointer during sampling without holding locks. We can do this because we run sampling in JavaThread and no safepoint can happen during sampling

pulls.title: 8392686: Don't attempt to reserve address space for compressed classes as unscaled or zero-based encoding with COH enabled
pulls.author: fthevenet
pulls.body_excerpt: When Compressed Object Headers are enabled, we don't benefit from the base for the encoding range for compressed classes being equal to `nullptr`, so there is no point in attempting to reserve a range that is optimized for that. This is, in effect, means that when reserving address space when COH are enabled, we should follow the same code path as when a CDS archive is used, as it doesn't attempt such optimization either. pulls.title: 8391909: Improve ConfinedSegmentPool Performance
pulls.author: minborg
pulls.body_excerpt: This PR proposes to improve the performance of the newly integrated confined arena cache. Confined arenas now remember the platform pool array and the pool array index used for pool acquisition. Upon closing the arena, the pool can be returned (in most cases) directly to the correct index in the confined arena cache. If the opportunistic pool index is occupied, the logic falls back to the regular path, which scans the array for an empty slot. The PR additionally proposes to add a test to make sure the unusual release path works correctly. --------- - [x] I confirm that I make this contribution

pulls.title: 8391914: x86: Optimize StringUTF16.compress intrinsic with AVX2
pulls.body_excerpt: Currently the StringUTF16.compress intrinsic (MacroAssembler::char_array_compress) intrinsic only has an AVX-512 path (gated by UseAVX > 2 && supports_avx512vlbw() && supports_bmi2()) and an SSE4.2 16-char path. Machines with AVX2 but no AVX-512 (or with AVX3Threshold > 0) fall back to the slower SSE4.2 path. This change adds a 32-char AVX2 loop for such CPUs. pulls.title: 8342870: Errors related to unused code on Windows after 8339120 in accessibility
pulls.author: TheShermanTanker
pulls.body_excerpt: After 8339120, gcc began catching many different instances of unused code in the Windows specific codebase. Some of these seem to be bugs. I've taken the effort to mark out all the relevant globals and locals that trigger the unused warnings and addressed all of them by commenting out the code as appropriate. I am confident that in many cases this simplistic approach of commenting out code does not fix the underlying issue, and the warning actually found a bug that should be fixed. In these instances, I will be aiming to fix these bugs with help from reviewers, so I recommend anyone reviewing
